correctness.rationale: The explicit sign-pair expansion gives \(\mathbb EF_a^2=2S_2/n\) and \(\mathbb EF_a^6=2[15S_2S_4+(n-16)S_6]/[n(n-1)]\). On the closed normalized-squares simplex, the exact identity \(15(u^2+v^2)-(16-n)(u^3+v^3)=15s^2-(16-n)s^3+3((16-n)s-10)uv\) supplies a complete pairwise variation argument. The proof rules out supports greater than two for maxima, forces uniform positive support at minima of size at least three, and compares the finite exceptional cases exactly. Compact signed-permutation averaging of quadratic comparison forms proves the claimed Banach--Mazur optimality. A standalone checker independently enumerated 420 exact rational sampled-sign cases, 99 dimensions of endpoints and additional identity cases; finite checks are corroboration, not infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Actual semantic queries of published mathematical records and previous documented theorem claims found nearby Rademacher, Walsh, and signed-rook moment statements but no equivalent signed two-site sixth-moment classification. Primary full-text comparisons show the main relevant literature either treats sparse sketch moment bounds, pairwise-independent nonzero signs, or sums with independent zero indicators. The new sharp dimension-four and dimension-six equality cases and exact Euclidean distortion are not implied by these inspected theorem statements. This conclusion is evidence-limited; absence from search is not uniqueness proof.
residual_risks: A general sharp theorem for exchangeable fixed-cardinality, sign-symmetric random vectors could imply the result under a different name, including material not indexed in searched literature.
The exact extremizer geometry for a two-sparse sampling distribution could be present in an unpublished table or appendix outside the inspected sources.

value.rationale: Exactly-two occupied coordinate sampling is the first nontrivial fixed-cardinality signed sparsification used as a building block in sparse randomized embeddings. Rather than selecting an arbitrary small dimension, the theorem classifies the entire family \(n\ge2\), exposes a nonstandard change in minimizing support at dimension four and a full plateau of maximizing two-coordinate ratios at dimension six, proves attained sharp constants and equality rigidity, and computes the optimal Euclidean distortion. This gives a precise norm-geometric benchmark for correlated sparse signs; no general downstream theorem is claimed.
